Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Considering the bug report mentioning an issue with the descendant-or-self axis at the root node, and the test using XPath query `//vendor`, there might be an issue with how JXPath handles the descendant-or-self axis at the root node.

messages.content:
The `assertXPathNodeType` method in the `JXPathTestCase` class sets the context to non-lenient, gets the pointer for the given XPath, and then checks whether the node class obtained by evaluating the XPath query is assignable from the expected class.

In this context, the issue mentioned in the bug report may be related to the handling of the descendant-or-self axis at the root node within the JXPath implementation.

To resolve this issue, it might be necessary to investigate how JXPath processes XPath queries involving the descendant-or-self axis at the root node and ensure that it returns the expected results.

Considering the information gathered so far, the possible fix could involve updating the XPath processing logic in JXPath to correctly handle descendant-or-self axis queries at the root node.

The ideal methods to be fixed are:
- `org.apache.commons.jxpath.JXPathContext.getPointer(java.lang.String)`
